data.narrative:
GenFab Co is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Matt Parlmer that has raised $510K to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of nine private firms and one public company in the Robotics & Manufacturing sector, including peers such as Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics.

The stage-progression method is applicable here and serves as the primary valuation anchor. Using total capital raised as a proxy for pre-money valuation and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $1.275M. The peer-median method could not be reliably applied due to insufficient narrow comparables—while 10 same-sector peers exist, fewer than three datapoints meet strict filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier positioning. Relying on all-sector medians at this stage would introduce unwarranted noise.

The analysis triangulates to a median valuation of $1.275M, with a low-end scenario of $1.08M and high-end of $1.47M, all approximately $1M. Key uncertainties include the thinness of truly comparable seed-stage robotics datasets and the stability of the 2.5x multiplier across this subsector. Given reliance on a single method, this range should be treated as directional rather than definitive. Additional data on recent seed rounds within the immediate peer set would strengthen conviction.
